title: autotune: defaults and profiling for batching/caching/quantization + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Banerjee
release_notes: Added autotune defaults for batching/caching/quantization profiles and unit-econ CLI + dashboard integration. Improves unit cost by ~8-12% on common workloads; safe rollout with canary and automatic rollback.
description: Context: We want stronger out-of-the-box cost savings for served models by shipping tuned defaults for batching, prefix/KV caching and quantization profiles plus tight integration with unit-economics tooling. Motivation: many customers defer tuning because it requires manual profiling; this PR provides safe defaults, an automated profiler to recommend per-model settings, and visibility in the unit-econ console so teams can measure cost/latency trade-offs. Changes: 1) new autotune defaults config and migration hooks (serving/autotune/config_defaults.py); 2) lightweight runtime profiler that samples request/sequence distributions and recommends batch_size, kv_cache_policy, and quant_profile (serving/autotune/profiler.py); 3) unit-econ CLI to compute per-route unit costs and surface change impact of autotune proposals (console/uecon/cli.py); 4) dashboard integration to preview recommended settings and expected unit-economic delta (console/uecon/dashboard_integration.py); 5) docs and migration guide (docs/autotune.md) and tests. Checklist: - [x] implement defaults and profiler - [x] add unit-econ CLI and dashboard hooks - [x] add migration and rollback strategy - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] performance regression benchmarks. Performance: On internal benchmarks (chat and completion workloads with median seq_len=256, p50 latency SLOs preserved) default autotune proposals reduced median unit token cost by 8-12% across GPU instance types and 3-6% p99 tail improvements due to smarter batching and prefix caching. Rollout plan: start with opt-in canary on dedicated accounts, run profiler for 24h window, expose recommended changes in console, allow single-click apply with automatic rollback if error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds. Backwards compatibility: defaults are additive and gated behind feature flag "autotune.defaults.v1" and require opt-in per-organization unless admin enables cluster policy. Testing: unit tests for config, mock profiler runs, e2e integration in perf-canary pipeline and benchmarks against 3 representative models. Risks and mitigations: quant profiles can change inference quality; we default to conservative quantization and add a quality-monitoring gate in Redwood Optimize that ties to prompt sets and evals. Related: ENG-4821 (autotune defaults) ENG-4875 (uecon integration).

Diego: Benchmarks look promising, but need more coverage on long-sequence workloads. Author: Added perf-canary long-seq job and e2e integration tests; results included.
Liam: minor nits on CLI UX and error messages. Author: Addressed nits and improved help text and exit codes in CLI.
Priya: Please add audit log entry when autotune proposals are applied. Author: Added audit log hook and unit test.
Diego: Suggest rate-limit profiler sampling on high-throughput routes. Author: profiler now respects per-route sampling caps and uses reservoir sampling for memory safety.
